A restaurant specializing in pizza
Located a 1-minute walk from Exit 1 of Sangsu Station.
A slice of pepperoni pizza costs 5,000 won.

Does pepperoni taste like this?
Luckily, I was able to receive freshly baked pizza.
One piece costs 5,000 won, so it feels expensive, but
It wasn't a waste of money when I ate it.
Especially because it’s freshly baked pizza.
The taste of the oil mixed with the meat was really good.
Plus the flavor of the rich tomato sauce~
It's amazing that you can feel such a stimulating taste.
Good for those who miss the taste of rich sauce!
The dough is thin, so the toppings and sauce are overflowing with flavor.
It would have been a shame if it had been thicker, but it was a good choice~
Especially if you fold the pizza in half, it’s double!!!
Better than the pizza for one person from a cheap pizza chain.
It seems to be much more cost-effective.
Of course, the taste of cold pizza may be different.

Store & Tips & Review
The store is not large, but there are quite a few tables.
Since it is a bar-type table, it is okay to eat alone.
However, since it is an open store, on days when there are a lot of bugs…
Order and pay at the counter.
If you don't have any pizza, they make it right away and it takes about 7 minutes.
Packaging is also possible, but only in paper boxes.
The problem is that when putting freshly baked pizza in it, oil leaks out.
If you put it in your bag, you'll probably shed tears of blood!
Be sure to hold it in your hand and eat it when the heat disappears.
There seem to be a few more stores besides here.
I felt satisfied even though I ate it after eating ramen for dinner!

One-shot course? It was the best taco I've ever had.

♤ Mixto Taco (corn tortilla) (4,500₩)
♤ Chorizo Taco (corn tortilla) (4,200₩)
♤ Badger Gamtu Quesa Taco (5,500₩)
♤ Madre Ensemble Mezcal (8,000₩)

I can't believe this violent taste was hidden in a small taco restaurant in Sangsu Station. You can choose between flour and corn tortillas for tacos, and I highly recommend ordering the corn tortillas because they are incredibly savory. The tortillas are delicious, but more than anything, the quality of the meat is amazing. Even though it has a fragrant oil, there is no smell of oil at all, and the moisture remains moist, making it really delicious. The salsa sauce that adds flavor is a bonus. The chorizo ​​was also spicy and soft, making it great.

Quesa tacos are tacos made by pressing cheese on a tortilla and grilling it. It was crispy, salty, and delicious, just like eating a cheese skirt burger from a famous burger restaurant. I recommend trying at least one quesa taco.

I tried mezcal, which is an agave distilled liquor, and it has a smokier and hotter taste than tequila.

I was wondering why so many people were raving about it, but it was worth it... I will definitely be visiting again!

reviews.author: Chanwook Lee
reviews.text:
According to the mejicanos I met while traveling, they say it's worth coming to Mexico just for the tacos, but I'm still dying to go. However, in the distant future, we have no choice but to eat diligently in Korea.

This is my first time visiting Sangsu-dong, where foreign restaurants are concentrated, to eat tacos. However, I haven't had a chance to buy and eat properly made tacos, so I stopped by this taqueria just to experience it.

I found out about this casual taqueria that seemed to target college students through word of mouth, and there were quite a few customers who came to eat alone. It was like a fast food restaurant where you can eat and drink quickly.

In fact, if you look at the interior, it looks like a Tex-Mex restaurant you would see in the U.S., but when I looked at the menu, I saw that it was focused on Mexican-style tacos. The set menu was well planned, so I ordered three tacos.

The taco set includes one drink, but if you pay an additional fee, it is changed to alcohol, so we start drinking tequila in broad daylight. I grabbed a shot of Jose Cuervo with lime and drank it straight, and it tasted like distilled white wine and was very good.

There are three tacos in the taco set: shoulder meat, mixto, and chorizo, and you can choose the tortilla, so I chose a corn tortilla. All of them are pork-based, except for the chorizo, and two of them are simmered in lard.

The shoulder taco had soft textured meat like pulled pork covered in salsa and topped with onions and cilantro. The rich meat flavor and moisture filled my mouth, and the coriander completely offset the heaviness.

The mixto taco was a combination of head meat, badger persimmon, and shoulder meat, so it was a taco in itself with soup. It had a very rich flavor and went well with corn tortillas, and the chewy texture of the badger persimmon added to its charm.

The chorizo ​​taco had a strong spice, so the cilantro flavor was strong, and the meat and chili oil were strong enough to ooze out through the tortilla. In the case of chorizo, it was excellent because it was crushed and had a moist texture and high moisture.

P.S. ¿Tacos in Corea? ¡Ahora mismo!

Downtowner Sangsu branch is located right in front of Sangsu Station and has great accessibility. If you wanted to eat a hamburger in Sangsu, it was a convenient place to meet without having to explain the location, so it was also a good meeting place. The store has a casual yet hip atmosphere, so I didn't feel out of place even if I came alone, and I felt comfortable visiting with friends or on a date.

This time, I had a classic cheeseburger and a cheeseburger, and the basics of both menus were really solid. The classic cheeseburger had a juicy patty and was well combined with crunchy and fresh vegetables, so it wasn't greasy, and the sauce had a good balance, so it was easy to eat cleanly until the end.
The cheeseburger has a stronger cheese flavor, so I think it would be a good fit for cheese lovers. The cheese blended naturally with the patty, and the more you chewed, the more savory it became.
I would like to especially recommend this to first-time visitors as it is a burger centered on the taste of meat.

The size of the hamburger was larger than I expected, so it was enough for a meal even without sides.
This is a place I would recommend as a fail-safe option when you want to eat a handmade burger in Sangsu, and I think I will visit again the next time I come to Sangsu.

If it's in the low 10,000 won range, it's a handmade burger that's less expensive.
A hamburger consists of a bun, patty, cheese, pickles, and sautéed onions.
The bun has a unique texture that is soft on top and crunchy on the bottom.
Maybe that’s why it has a fun texture that goes well with the crispy patty!
Cheddar and mozzarella? The combination of white and yellow has a good visual due to the inclusion of these two ingredients.
However, the taste is ambiguous, perhaps because the flavors cancel each other out.
There is sauce and rich cheese, but why does the seasoning feel weak and bland to me?

The visuals were really nice, but it was a bit far from the cheeseburger flavor I expected.
The fries are a bit thick and seasoned, so those who like seasoned potatoes are welcome.

Drinks are served in cans, which I like.

Store & Tips & Review

reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
The hamburger at the COEX branch Burger Plant, which I stopped by and tasted out of curiosity after hearing that Shinsegae CEO Jeong Yong-jin had launched it, was pretty good, so I hoped it would become Korea's representative premium franchise hamburger brand with a cooked-to-order system that is a step above the typical McDonald's-style pre-cooked franchise hamburger restaurants.

Mos Burger, a similar type of Japanese representative, has its own charm, but when it comes to hamburgers, Koreans prefer American tastes rather than Japanese tastes. It is close to American tastes, but they used a sauce with a slightly sweet taste that Koreans like, so I visited the COEX branch and Nonhyeon branch occasionally, but it may not have been as popular with Koreans as I expected. The Nonhyeon branch did not have many customers when I visited. It was a shame.

Meanwhile, a No Brand Burger recently appeared near Hongdae. I wondered what a No Brand Burger was, but I was curious and decided to visit because the No Brand store seemed to be a bit hotter than Burger Plant because it had higher brand awareness and offered cheaper prices.

The store was of a certain size, but I thought it was a bigger store because it became an issue, but it wasn't that big.

The store was decorated using white, black, and yellow, the colors of the No Brand store, and the method was to order from the kiosk on the left after entering the store.

I didn't come to eat, but stopped by just because I was curious about what kind of burger it tasted like, so I ordered the most basic menu item, NBB Original, and sat at the bar table to wait. My order number was displayed on the screen above the kiosk, so I came to my seat holding a tray with the hamburger I ordered on it.

The burger wrapped in paper was not as thick as the picture at other hamburger restaurants, but was about the size of a Burger King Whopper Junior. When I opened the paper and looked at it, it turned out to be like a Whopper Junior, with a hamburger bun studded with sesame seeds, a patty, onions, tomatoes, lettuce, and two types of sauce (white and cheese).

When I took a bite, I immediately thought of it as a Whopper Junion, as I saw in someone's review. It felt a little different than the Whopper Junior because of the taste of the sauce, which was slightly sweeter, but it felt very similar since the patties were grilled using the same direct fire grilling method as Burger King.

Burger Plant also grilled the patties over an open fire, but it didn't have the Whopper Junior feel like the ones here. The burgers were okay for the price, but it felt like the original feel of this restaurant had been lost, which was a bit disappointing.

I was curious about whether all Burger Plants would change to No Brand Burger, so I called Burger Plant's Nonhyeon branch to inquire, and they said that the COEX branch was being renovated as a No Brand Burger store, and that the Nonhyeon branch would continue to be Burger Plant for the time being.

There were many different burger menus, and based on the NBB Original Burger I tried this time, it was overall excellent value for money, but it did not have the characteristics of a No Brand Burger and felt like a copy of the Whopper Junior, which was a disappointing visit, so I am not sure if I will visit again.

This is a self-service buffet-style pizza restaurant. You can enjoy unlimited pizza, salad, and various sub menus for 13,000 won for lunch on weekdays, 16,000 won for dinner, and 18,000 won on weekends and holidays. (The packaging says all pizzas are 9,900 won, but I've never tried packaging, so I'm not sure about that.)

First of all, the pizza is of good quality. It's not a special pizza, it's just pizza baked using a regular machine, but since it's baked and served right away, you can eat a variety of pizzas to your heart's content. You can also eat unlimited salads and drinks, as well as waffles, ice cream, shaved ice, and snacks. Considering the price, it is a very luxurious assortment. However, pizza is freshly baked when it comes out right away, but when it's on display, all you have to do is gently heat it with a heating element, etc., so it may harden when it cools. It's a good idea to aim for pizza that comes out right away.

The space is quite spacious and well decorated, creating a modern atmosphere. You can use the 2nd and 3rd floors, but the buffet is mainly located on the 2nd floor and there is no elevator, so you have to walk. There is no separate serving and it is basic self-service.

Currently (October 2024), if you write a review on Naver, you are offered unlimited beer service. The beer nozzles were well maintained and the draft beer tasted good.

Since this is an area where many students come and go, I hope that this cost-effective store will prosper.

Hongdae was unfamiliar to me, so I followed a cafe my friend suggested I go to. It was said to be a large cafe with lots of plants and a terrace, and the exterior of the cafe was pretty. It was also great for taking pictures.

It was so hot outside that I had to wait for a seat to become available, but luckily it did happen quickly. Since there are a lot of seats, the turnover rate seems to be good.

In addition to teas, the menu has a wide variety of ade, juice, smoothies, shaved ice, highballs, cocktails, wine, sangria, and beer. Perhaps because it was a hot day, there were especially many people eating shaved ice.

Add shot/add milk +1,000 won
Americano refill +1,500 won
Decaffeinated +500 won
Non-fat milk/oat milk change +500 won

There are 7 types of cakes for dessert, as well as other bakery items such as croissants and salt bread.

Colin Cafe has many plants both outside and inside, and they also sell flowers. It would also be great to go on a date. In addition to bouquets and dried flowers, there are also cacti.

I took a seat on the second floor, but I sat on the terrace and then moved inside. The terrace was pretty, but it was a little hot.

The restrooms are located inside the store, separated for men and women, and are clean, but it was a bit disappointing that there was only one toilet. The cafe is large, but there are so many people that there is bound to be a line. I think it would be okay when there are few customers.

My companion ordered an Americano (6,000 won) and I ordered a latte (6,500 won) with decaf (500 won). I thought it would be nice if the amount was a little larger, but this was just about right. If I had known then, I would have refilled the Americano, but I found out while writing this.

It was perfect because the store was cool, and there were knee blankets for those who get cold a lot. It was a cafe with a nice atmosphere.

reviews.author: Gundong Lee
reviews.text:
A flower oasis found in an alley in Hongdae – COLLINE cafe review

When you walk from Hongdae Entrance Station towards Sangsu Station,
At some point, the scent of flowers and the neat interior catches your eye, making you wonder, ‘What is here?’
That's COLLINE (Colin).
It’s a cafe that seems to capture ‘the one emotion you never knew would come’ in one space.

⸻

1. Entrance feeling that you fall in love with at first sight

Rich hydrangeas and plant interior visible through the glass door,
And a neat wooden sign.
The desire to take pictures is overwhelming.
There may be a waiting line on weekends, so we recommend right after opening or in the evening!

⸻

2. The signature drink is a must-try

The menu item I loved was definitely the Cotton Latte.
The fragrant coffee scent wafts over the soft foam like cotton candy.
And the Hongsi Shaved Ice, which is available as a summer-only menu, is a special treat that can only be experienced now.
The combination of sweet and soft syrup and ice leaves an emotional mark.

⸻

3. Not just a “good place to take pictures,” but a place you want to stay

When you sit on the terrace on the first floor, the sensibility of the streets of Sangsu unfolds before your eyes.
From the window seat on the second floor, the view of the back alleys of Hongdae is like a painting.
I like the moment when I can feel that feeling in my body rather than capturing it in a photo.

⸻

4. A tip
• Recommended photo route: Signboard –> (view of the terrace) –> 2nd floor window –> close-up of drink
• If the wait is long, the second floor is less crowded and has more atmosphere.
• It’s a great course for a light brunch or date, and it’s a ‘must-do course’ if you’re looking to take emotional photos.

⸻

Overall review

Colin is worthy of the expression, “A small garden in Hongdae and a glass of emotion.”
Not just a ‘pretty cafe’,
It is a space that adds an emotion that cannot be overlooked.
Next time, I want to come back when the seasonal sensibility changes rather than hydrangeas.

Although there were not many different flavors, the taste was solid and I, who has a dull sense of taste, was satisfied.

Barley barley rice / It was delicious because I could feel the savory taste of roasted barley. I am not a person who knows what flavor risotto tastes like, but I enjoyed this.

Lemon dill butter / The butter tasted just right, sour and had a good dill scent. It doesn't have a subtle buttery taste like others (such as Scooper), but a clear buttery taste.

Salted Milk / This was a gelato that clearly felt like it had salt mixed in. Usually, there are a lot of cases where salty flavors (salty caramel/salty chocolate/salty milk) taste salty or not, but here, the subtle salty taste went well with the sweetness and was nice.

Kiwi flavor / It reminded me of the ice cream sticks sold at the supermarket back in the day, but it tasted better than that, and it was a bit surprising because it was sweeter and didn't bite. The tomato basil flavor was good, and the chocolate milk flavor wasn't as good as the Valrhona chocolate gelato, but it didn't taste like Jetty milk and was a decent taste. It wasn't that sweet so it suited my taste.
